query_preparation.promotion_rule: Official map/API/register/download capability may be VERIFIED or PREPARED_QUERY, but exact candidate result remains PENDING_RAW_RESPONSE until candidate-specific spatial/address/asset/record evidence and provenance are captured.

batches.c: BGS GeoIndex supports map navigation, query, clip/download and borehole/geology layers. Exact candidate spatial selection is required; map presence is screening evidence only.
SOBI contains over one million borehole/shaft/well records and is suitable for site-level screening. Nearest borehole is not the candidate ground investigation.
BGS Geology 50K is local-to-regional geological mapping. Exact candidate polygon binding is required and mapping does not replace intrusive ground investigation.
GeoIndex/Geology services can separate bedrock and superficial context. Generalised map units must not be promoted as verified site strata without local records.
Borehole logs may originate from historic site investigations and vary in age/content. Record identity, coordinate and log provenance must be preserved.
GeoIndex exposes engineering geology and hazard-related layers. These are screening inputs and not a foundation design or geotechnical conclusion.
Different BGS products have different scales, access and licence conditions. A coarser/open layer must not be silently substituted for a more detailed site product.
The statutory biodiversity metric is the official BNG calculation method. Candidate scoring requires site habitat parcels, condition and exact red-line area.
Mandatory BNG uses pre/post habitat units and a 10% gain target where applicable. Eligibility/exemptions and scheme facts must be resolved before liability.
The metric treats habitat parcels inside the development red line separately. Candidate point coordinates alone cannot establish habitat area or condition.
Natural England's Ancient Woodland dataset is spatial and current as of April 2026. Exact intersection is required; revised inventory takes precedence where applicable.
Where a county has revised Ancient Woodland inventory data, revised information should supersede the older inventory. Dataset vintage must be retained.
Strategic significance is one statutory metric factor. It requires the correct local strategy/context and cannot be inferred from borough name alone.
Official mapping can identify candidate habitat context, but habitat type and condition for the metric normally require site evidence; no biodiversity units are invented.
UKCP Local provides high-resolution projections; candidate use requires the correct grid, variable, scenario and time slice rather than a borough average.
Mean/max/min temperature projections are scenario outputs, not forecasts. Scenario, baseline and ensemble member must be retained.
Rainfall projections require careful dataset choice and caveat handling; projected rainfall does not equal a site drainage design value.
Met Office warns about unrealistic extreme rainfall features in some UKCP Local simulations. Affected hourly data must not be used uncritically for decisions.
Met Office recommends considering more than one 5km grid box for local estimates. A single grid cell should not be treated as precise parcel climate.

batches.t: London Climate Risk Map LSOA context gate
batches.c: GLA climate-risk mapping combines climate exposure with social vulnerability. It is neighbourhood context, not a parcel physical-risk measurement.
Future climate projections inform adaptation planning but do not describe current site conditions or guarantee a future event at the candidate.
ORR station usage is station-level official statistics. Exact nearest/relevant station identity and access route are required before candidate association.
The latest station-usage release currently covers April 2024-March 2025; the 2025-26 release is scheduled for November 2026.
Station usage is estimated mainly from ticket sales and includes methodological adjustments. Estimates are not direct footfall counters at the candidate.
Entries/exits and interchanges are distinct measures and must not be combined without preserving meaning.
ORR's latest passenger rail usage covers January-March 2026 and reports network-level journeys; it is broader context, not station demand.
Regional rail usage and station usage operate at different geographies. Regional growth cannot be assigned directly to one candidate station.

batches.t: TfL Cycling Infrastructure Database proximity prep
batches.c: TfL CID covers cycle lanes/tracks, parking, crossings, modal filters and other cycling assets across Greater London. Exact asset proximity/type is required.
Signed routes, lanes, tracks, crossings and parking are different infrastructure classes and must not be collapsed into one availability flag.
DfT walking/cycling statistics support area trends but are not designed to evaluate individual local schemes or candidate-site behaviour.
CWIS3 sets 2026 government active-travel objectives and 2035 targets. Targets are policy context, not delivered infrastructure at a candidate.
Council funding allocations indicate planned delivery capacity; they do not prove a route/crossing exists beside the candidate.
No active-travel score is promoted without exact network/asset relation and suitable route-quality evidence.
National heat-network zoning modelling identifies opportunity areas, not automatically designated zones. Exact zone status/effectivity must be preserved.
DESNZ's 2026 pipeline review concerns future prioritised potential zones before statutory zoning implementation; pipeline inclusion is not current designation.
The Heat Networks Planning Database tracks projects through inception, planning, construction, operation and decommissioning. Exact project and status are required.
HNPD is updated after each quarter; the current dataset identified is February-April 2026, published July 2026. Status date must be retained.
Heat Networks (Market Framework) Regulations 2026 introduced Ofgem regulation. Regulatory status does not prove network availability to a candidate.
A planned/in-construction heat network is not operational capacity. Candidate connection potential remains pending exact network and provider evidence.
Opportunity mapping and project proximity do not establish connection cost, capacity, timing or mandatory connection for a scheme.
Ofcom Spring 2026 provides a January 2026 snapshot of fixed broadband availability. Exact premise/address coverage is required for a candidate.
Gigabit-capable availability is a service-coverage measure and not proof of a specific supplier contract, capacity or installation lead time.
Ofcom mobile coverage is based on operator signal-strength predictions. It has uncertainty at specific locations and must remain prediction-labelled.
5G non-standalone and standalone coverage are distinct. Candidate connectivity evidence must preserve technology and confidence level.
Ofcom's 2026 planned deployment report reflects operator plans to January 2029. Plans are not current availability and may change.
Local-authority or national coverage percentages cannot be converted into a candidate connectivity score without exact premise checker evidence.
EA permitted waste-site data contains granted permit records. Exact candidate distance/intersection and permit status are required.
Authorised landfill boundaries are current permitted-site polygons. Exact spatial relation is required and does not imply contamination at the candidate.
Current authorised landfill and historic landfill datasets serve different purposes. Closed/removed sites must not be treated as operational.
Landfill datasets include different descriptor/permit classes. Waste type and regulatory status must be retained.
EA landfill summaries are updated quarterly; the end-March 2026 dataset was published May 2026. Retrieval and reporting period must be preserved.
Proximity to a permitted waste site is contextual evidence only; it is not a parcel contamination, nuisance or viability conclusion without further evidence.
